nodes.label: Monthly rolling-origin backtest (2018-03 to 2018-08)
nodes.description: 38,988 test orders; each model trains only on orders whose delivery was known before the test month; metrics macro-averaged per month (DD-09).

nodes.label: August 2018 delivery promise change (concept drift)
nodes.description: 75% of August 2018 orders promised in under 20 days; relationship between promise length and lateness reversed; lift fell to 1.2x.
nodes.rationale: Most important moving part found in the dataset; a monitor on the distribution of promised days would catch it.

nodes.label: Late-delivery model (v1 logistic regression)
nodes.description: Logistic regression on 16 numeric + 3 categorical features, one delivered order, label fact_orders.is_late (8.1% positive), predicted at purchase. PR-AUC 0.184, ROC-AUC 0.707, Brier 0.0778; top 10% flagged precision 0.207, catches 27.9% of late orders; lift 2.8x average, 1.2x in Aug 2018.
nodes.rationale: Intended for triage by rank (flag riskiest share), not quoting probabilities; probabilities off in level by ~0.06/month because monthly late rate swings 1.4%-21.4%.

nodes.label: Weekly order forecast
nodes.description: Orders per ISO week from fact_orders, 85 clean weeks 2017-01-02 to 2018-08-13; rolling origin from week 26 (59 one-week, 56 four-week forecasts). Recommendation: average of naive and 8-week MA at 1 week (MAE 183 vs 204 naive), 8-week MA at 4 weeks (272 vs 353).
nodes.rationale: Combination assembled after seeing results so its edge is optimistic; ranking of complex models unstable (AR(1) good on revenue, bad on orders) so 85 weeks cannot separate them; simple averages recommended.

nodes.label: Always-predict-training-late-rate baseline
nodes.description: PR-AUC 0.085, ROC-AUC 0.500.

nodes.label: Seller own-history rate baseline
nodes.description: PR-AUC 0.099.

nodes.label: Gradient boosting baseline
nodes.description: PR-AUC 0.172 vs logistic 0.184; worse than the linear model.

nodes.label: Grouped permutation importance
nodes.description: PR-AUC lost when shuffled: route 0.076, promise 0.063, basket 0.005, seller history 0.005, payment 0.001, weekday/hour 0.000.
nodes.rationale: Model is essentially where the parcel goes and how long the customer was promised; in Aug 2018 shuffling route raised PR-AUC by 0.06 as the learned geography no longer held.

nodes.label: ML layer (src/ml, sql/ml)
nodes.description: late_delivery_features.sql builds point-in-time features; late_delivery_baseline.py and forecast_baseline.py run rolling-origin backtests writing metrics to reports/.

nodes.label: August 2018 delivery-promise policy shift
nodes.rationale: 72% of non-canceled August orders were promised in under 20 days with a 13.9% late rate; concept drift in a plain v1 feature (promised days, within-month ROC-AUC 0.186) that made August the weakest month for every model. Cause of the policy change is not in the data.

nodes.label: E2: persistence of route/category/seller lateness
nodes.rationale: Routes are stable P2 to P3 (Spearman 0.70, near noise ceiling 0.85); categories are not; sellers persist only P2 to P3.

nodes.label: E5: oracle true month late rate ceiling
nodes.norm_label: e5: oracle true month late rate ceiling
nodes.rationale: Giving the model the true month rate leaves PR-AUC unchanged (0.1837 to 0.1839) while Brier drops 9% (0.0778 to 0.0711): system drift is a calibration problem, not a ranking problem.

nodes.label: E6: route history redundant with state and distance
nodes.norm_label: e6: route history redundant with state and distance
nodes.rationale: Without geography route history recovers half of the lost 0.067 PR-AUC, but on top of full v1 it lowers PR-AUC by ~0.009: informative and stable yet already present in v1.

nodes.label: v4: relative route/category rate features
nodes.rationale: Beat v2 in all four windows by 0.002 to 0.011 but never beat v1.

nodes.label: Features v2: route and category late-rate history
nodes.norm_label: features v2: route and category late-rate history
nodes.rationale: Slightly worse (PR-AUC 0.174); route history repeats state and distance already in v1.

nodes.label: Features v3: trailing 28-day system late rate
nodes.norm_label: features v3: trailing 28-day system late rate
nodes.rationale: Worse (0.178); recent late rate does not predict the next month's.

nodes.label: Features v5: delivery-time slack
nodes.rationale: No gain (0.176 vs 0.184); top-quintile calibration somewhat closer (0.191 predicted vs 0.165 actual).

nodes.label: Recalibration on latest resolved orders
nodes.rationale: Worse on Brier, log loss and calibration error; holding orders out made the base model staler.

nodes.label: Use the model by rank, not probability
nodes.norm_label: use the model by rank, not probability
nodes.rationale: Operating point is a share of orders flagged (e.g. riskiest 10%); fairness review needed if used to affect customers because state drives ranking.

nodes.label: Shorter / walk-forward training windows
nodes.rationale: +0.010 PR-AUC but wins in only 3 of 6 months, mostly August; a fixed 2-month window looked best only in hindsight (0.205).

nodes.label: Forecast baselines: naive, moving averages, linear trend
nodes.norm_label: forecast baselines: naive, moving averages, linear trend

nodes.label: Gradient boosting baseline (depth 4)
nodes.rationale: Did not beat the linear model (PR-AUC 0.172 vs 0.184), so improvement is more likely from better features than a bigger model.

nodes.label: Seller history rate baseline
nodes.rationale: ROC-AUC 0.526, near coin flip: late deliveries cluster in time more than they stick to sellers.

nodes.label: v2: route and category late-rate history features
nodes.norm_label: v2: route and category late-rate history features
nodes.rationale: Logistic PR-AUC fell to 0.174; extra history made the model more confident without making it more right. Later shown redundant with v1 state and distance columns.

nodes.label: v3: trailing 28-day system late rate feature
nodes.norm_label: v3: trailing 28-day system late rate feature
nodes.rationale: Logistic PR-AUC 0.178, Brier 0.0859; drift analysis showed it tracks regime, with within-month ROC-AUC 0.446 on test.

nodes.label: Recalibration experiment (level shift, Platt, isotonic)
nodes.rationale: No variant beat the reference on Brier, log loss or calibration error: recent late rate does not predict next month's, and holding orders out for calibration makes the base model staler (PR-AUC 0.184 to 0.176/0.166).

nodes.label: Training-window tuning experiment
nodes.rationale: 2-month window looked best (0.205) only in hindsight; walk-forward choice gained +0.010 PR-AUC, won 3 of 6 months, +0.070 in August 2018 alone; chosen window jumped 3,4,6,6,2,2.

nodes.label: D-007: ML target is late delivery plus weekly order forecast
nodes.norm_label: d-007: ml target is late delivery plus weekly order forecast
nodes.rationale: Late-delivery label comes straight from timestamps, features at purchase are concrete (seller, product size, freight, route, promised window), and late orders drive reviews (2.57 vs 4.29 stars). Positive class 8.1% so PR metrics needed. Rejected low review score (highest leakage risk) and repeat purchase (~3.1% positives, censored window).

nodes.label: DD-08: Add scikit-learn for the ML baselines
nodes.norm_label: dd-08: add scikit-learn for the ml baselines
nodes.rationale: Standard well-tested logistic regression and gradient boosting; a baseline that has to be debugged is a poor baseline. Rejected hand-written models and rate-only baselines. statsmodels, lightgbm, xgboost not added.

nodes.label: DD-09: Report backtest metrics as per-month macro-average
nodes.norm_label: dd-09: report backtest metrics as per-month macro-average
nodes.rationale: Pooling test orders gave the constant baseline ROC-AUC 0.36 because pooling ranks different months' constants against each other; late rate swings 1.4% to 21.4% by month. Rejected pooled metrics.

nodes.label: DD-10: Keep v1 features as reference late-delivery model
nodes.norm_label: dd-10: keep v1 features as reference late-delivery model
nodes.rationale: v2 (route/category history) and v3 (trailing 28-day late rate) lowered logistic PR-AUC from 0.184 to 0.174 and 0.178 and worsened calibration. A model should not get more complex without a measured gain. v2/v3 kept in SQL for re-run.

nodes.label: Interview readiness decisions to defend
nodes.description: Why DuckDB/no cloud; why star schema and facts never join to facts; why predict at purchase; why stop improving the model; why rank not probability.

nodes.label: Total cloud cost $0
nodes.rationale: Everything runs locally on open-source tools (DuckDB, scikit-learn, uv, pytest, free Power BI Desktop); BigQuery, Dataflow, Vertex AI pricing never verified (Phase 0 sec 10).

nodes.label: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence
nodes.rationale: Data and anything derived (warehouse, features, model artefacts, Power BI exports) is non-commercial, needs attribution and must be shared under the same licence; drives git-ignoring data/ and powerbi/data/.

nodes.label: Security posture (local batch, no network surface)
nodes.norm_label: security posture (local batch, no network surface)
nodes.rationale: No server, accounts or cloud resources so most attack surface does not exist; checked 2026-10-13: no secrets, no tracked data/credentials, no hard-coded paths, no network calls in project code.

nodes.label: Raw data in early commits of public repo
nodes.norm_label: raw data in early commits of public repo
nodes.rationale: Repo garcane/GCP is public (checked 2026-10-15) so nine raw files are downloadable from commits before d8f6954; allowed with attribution; rewrite is owner's decision (D-008).

nodes.label: D-002: Local only, no GCP
nodes.rationale: Removes cost, credential risk and setup time; cloud adds no evidence for the data model and ML work. Rejected local-then-cloud (cost, scope) and emulators (setup without evidence). Trade-off: no cloud deployment to show; Dataflow/Beam and BigQuery region moot; cloud pricing stays unverified.

nodes.label: D-004: No dbt; plain SQL run by a Python script
nodes.norm_label: d-004: no dbt; plain sql run by a python script
nodes.rationale: Fewer moving parts; build order is small and explicit. Trade-off: no dbt lineage graph, docs site or built-in tests; table constraints and checks.sql cover the same ground.

nodes.label: D-006: .gitignore covers database, data/ and credentials
nodes.norm_label: d-006: .gitignore covers database, data/ and credentials
nodes.rationale: Database is rebuilt from source, raw data is re-downloadable, credentials must never be committed. Ignores *.duckdb, data/, .env*, *.pem, *.key, credential JSON, caches.

nodes.label: D-008: Untrack data/ from Git; do not rewrite history
nodes.norm_label: d-008: untrack data/ from git; do not rewrite history
nodes.rationale: Stops future commits carrying a CC BY-NC-SA dataset without a destructive force-push history rewrite (commit d8f6954). Trade-off: early commits still contain the raw files in a public repository.

nodes.label: Lesson: reconciliation checks pay for themselves
nodes.norm_label: lesson: reconciliation checks pay for themselves
nodes.rationale: 22 checks catch nothing dramatic, which is the point; analytics tables tie back to facts.

nodes.label: Lesson: decide scope early and write it down
